card.name: Endings of generic drug names
card.fires_on: The last piece of a generic drug name, such as -ine, -ole, -ene or -ium, just before a salt or dosage form word. Seen mostly in dosage sections.

modes.label: Name ending before salt
modes.description: Final piece of a drug name right before hydrochloride, sodium or chloride.
modes.example: 2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION Apply a thin layer of naftif<<ine>> hydrochloride gel, 2%

modes.label: Ending before dosage form
modes.description: Final piece of a drug name before solution, capsule or similar.
modes.example: DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION The usual dose is one drop of Carteol<<ol>> Hydrochloride Ophthalmic Solution

card.plain: It marks the point where a drug's generic name is finishing, so a salt or form word comes next.
